the thousands estimate is attributed to an external expert and refers to the broader supporter scene."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0005-E018","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A Diakonie-DIW expertise published in August 2023 stated that the coalition had been arguing for months over the child basic income, while describing it as a central government social-policy project and discussing child poverty's costs in health, education, and social participation.","notes":["The excerpt says the coalition had been arguing for months but does not explicitly state that this dispute delayed the concrete design."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0005-E019","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The €110–120 billion figure is presented by Diakonie President Ulrich Lilie as an implication of the cited OECD estimate, not as a separately quoted OECD figure."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0005-E020","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The modeled reduction is expressed as a possibility: the €100 transfer could reduce the share of affected households most among the scenarios."]}]}
